summary: Intermittent multi-second pause at stream start — windowed soft-throttling + client retries amplifying latency for BrightLogix
description:
Issue summary: BrightLogix (dedicated customer) reports intermittent multi-second pauses at the start of streamed responses. Customers see an apparent model hang for 3–8 seconds at stream initiation; after the pause either the stream resumes normally or the client issues immediate retries. Impact: user-facing latency spikes in production UI, elevated request counts and 429 responses, and customer concerns about model regression. Environment: prod-us-east serving dedicated pool (tenant brightlogix-dedicated). Steps to reproduce:
1) Use BrightLogix client in production traffic pattern (concurrent short-chat sessions, many small tokens).
2) Start streaming request (chat/completion) to the streaming endpoint pinned to redwood-open-7b-v2.
3) Observe initial delay between connection and first data frame, then either recovery or immediate client retry behavior.
Observed behavior: 3–8s pause at stream start in ~0.8% of sessions during traffic peaks; follow-up retries amplify request rate and quickly trigger soft rate-limiter enforcement returning 429s. Expected behavior: streams should begin delivering tokens within 200–800ms under normal load. Initial hypothesis: windowed soft-quota enforcement at per-tenant rate limiter is deferring requests without explicit Retry-After, combined with SDK/client immediate retry behavior causing amplification.
Logs and traces: attached traces show long wait inside streaming-proxy queue (trace IDs: trace-20260312-1405-79a, trace-20260312-1412-cf3). Rate-limiter logs for tenant show bursts reaching soft_quota_window limit and then a short enforced delay (soft_defer) rather than immediate 429; downstream clients interpret socket pause as a timeout and retry. No model-side OOMs or GPU saturation observed.
Impact notes: Because BrightLogix is on a dedicated pool, increased retries temporarily increased tail latency for co-located tenants by consuming the limited burst tokens in the shared per-pool limiter.
Attachments: excerpted proxy trace, rate-limiter event log, sample client SDK logs (obfuscated).
comments: 2026-03-12 15:03 — Asha Patel: Customer reported initial incident. Collected sample traces and asked for SDK version and example request pattern.

2026-03-12 16:01 — BrightLogix (Elena, eng lead): We see a pause right after the connect frame; our frontend retries immediately after 1s by default. This started after last week's traffic spike. Key urgency: impacts user UX and sometimes results in duplicate messages.

2026-03-12 18:20 — Diego Martinez (SRE): Confirmed traces. I can repro on a load test that mimics their short-session pattern. Pinpointed queueing in streaming-proxy; rate-limiter marks show "soft_defer" events at the same timestamps.

2026-03-13 09:11 — Lina Park (SDK): Noted that current JS SDK retry default is 1s fixed backoff for streaming connection failures. Raising immediate concern about amplification; recommended switching to jittered exponential backoff.

2026-03-13 13:45 — Diego Martinez: Temporarily increased tenant burst tokens in rate-limiter for brightlogix-dedicated to reduce customer impact while we investigate. Observed reduction in stream-start lull incidents during the window.
2026-03-14 10:30 — Asha Patel: Customer confirmed UX improvement after temporary increase but requests permanent fix and guidance on SDK settings.
2026-03-14 14:05 — Diego Martinez: Rolling change to include Retry-After header on 429 responses for streaming endpoints (infra PR linked).
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 17:00 — Reproduced locally with a synthetic load generator that opens many short-lived streaming sessions; observed identical 3–6s pause at stream start under bursty arrival patterns.

2026-03-12 19:10 — Rate-limiter configuration for dedicated pools uses a 'soft_quota_window' of 10s with a deferred accept path that causes the streaming-proxy to keep the connection open while tokens are delayed; no Retry-After header was previously emitted for deferred requests.

2026-03-12 20:50 — SDK default backoff (1s fixed) causes many clients to retry quickly; retries arrive within the same soft_quota_window and exhaust available burst tokens, flipping enforcement to hard 429s.
2026-03-13 11:30 — Serving runtime metrics: no increased GPU utilization or model-level latency regression; tail latency source is queuing in streaming-proxy and rate-limiter decision path.

2026-03-13 15:00 — Hypothesis validated: when the proxy delays initial data frames due to soft_defer semantics, clients interpret the stall as a failure and retry; combined effect results in ephemeral 429 storms and perceived inference timeouts.

2026-03-14 09:00 — Proposed immediate mitigations tested in staging: (1) emit Retry-After header on 429/deferred responses, (2) reduce soft_quota_window from 10s to 2s for short-session workloads, (3) add per-stream token accounting to avoid long-held reservations.
2026-03-14 11:20 — Observed that temporary bump of BrightLogix tenant burst reduced visible incidents; confirms rate-limiter as root contributor rather than model regression.
2026-03-14 13:00 — Identified infra PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2843) that implements Retry-After and short-window config with feature flag for canary rollout.
resolution: Mitigation applied: short-term — increased per-tenant burst allocation for brightlogix-dedicated and advised the customer to configure SDK to use jittered exponential backoff (documentation snippet and example provided). Short-term change reduced incidents immediately. Medium-term — merged infra PR to emit Retry-After on 429/deferred responses for streaming endpoints and reduce soft_quota_window for short-session detection; canary rollout started in us-east on 2026-03-14. Long-term actions — implement per-stream token accounting to avoid long-lived holds, instrument per-tenant streaming proxy queue depth and expose alerting, and update SDK defaults to jittered exponential backoff for streaming connection errors. Follow-ups: 1) Ops to monitor canary for 72 hours and report metrics (owner: Diego Martinez). 2) SDK team to ship minor release v0.12.4 with backoff default changes and sample config (owner: Lina Park). 3) Postmortem and runbook update to be published under linked confluence page (owner: Asha Patel).
